title: introduce-workload-aware-onboard-hints-and-changelog-microdiffs
author: Maya Patel
description: Context: onboarding teams frequently provide only a single canonical performance profile and a sparse README. For real workloads we observed wide variance in latency/cost per token across request patterns (short chat vs. long generation vs. embeddings sampling). This PR adds two complementary features: (1) workload-aware onboard hints — a compact artifact produced during model intake that recommends 2–4 profile presets (latency-first, cost-first, balanced, embed-optimized) plus batch/caching defaults derived from sampled traces; and (2) changelog microdiffs — a small structured summary that surfaces the subset of release-note-relevant profile changes (kernel choices, quantization presets, sample-rate assumptions, KV-cache compatibility) so release notes can be concise and actionable. Motivation: reduce time-to-production for new models, lower first-week cost surprises, and enable concise automated release notes for platform and customer-facing change feeds. Implementation: (a) intake recorder: lightweight trace sampler runs with a configured TTL (default 10k requests or 6h) inside onboarding harness; traces are normalized to workload categories and summarized via quantiles. (b) hint generator: rule-based + small heuristic scorer that maps trace signatures to suggested profile presets and flags risky knobs (e.g., beam size > 1, mixed-precision fallbacks). The hints are emitted as a compact YAML artifact alongside the model manifest. (c) microdiff generator: when a new profile or manifest is uploaded, we compute a semantic diff limited to 12 canonical keys (hardware affinity, quantization, kernel family, sequence-length buckets, batching defaults, kv-cache policy, prefills, seed prompts) and render both a short natural-language blurb and a machine-consumable microdiff JSON (compact). (d) UX surface: console preview and a CLI flag --preview-hints for onboarding engineers to inspect suggestions. Testing and validation: unit tests for sampler normalization, integration tests on 6 representative models (small to LLM scale) comparing suggested presets vs. historical best-effort baselines, and a canary rollout to the staging index that records cost delta estimates. Backwards compatibility: microdiffs are additive and produced only when manifest schema v2+ is used; legacy manifests are left unchanged. Rollout plan: staged — feature gated behind org flag model_onboard_hints; monitor cost/latency deltas and adoption metrics for 2 weeks before org-wide enable. Security/privacy: traces are sampled and stripped of prompt content; only timestamps, token lengths, and hardware telemetry are kept. Ops notes: added a curator lint to fail when suggested hints contradict explicit user overrides. Related work: follows ideas in ENG-1145 (profiling contract) and complements prior onboarding heuristics but focuses on compact, human-friendly suggestions and concise release microdiffs.
commits: refactor(onboard): factor intake-trace recorder and expose SampleNormalizer
feat(onboard): implement workload-hint generator and preset templates
feat(changelog): microdiff engine + natural-language blurb renderer
test(onboard): add integration harness and sample fixtures for 6 model families
docs(onboard): CLI preview docs and console preview screenshots
chore(ci): add canary job and lint rule for hint/override contradictions
diff_highlights: recorder.py: new lightweight sampling loop with reservoir sampler and normalization pipeline (≈200 lines)
generator.py: rule set mapping quantile signatures to profile presets; includes cost-estimator hooks
templates.yaml: added 4 preset templates with recommended batching and kv-cache defaults
engine.py: semantic key whitelist for microdiffs, comparator tolerant to key order and numeric epsilons
renderer.py: short blurb templating (max 280 chars) and machine microdiff output
onboard_preview.py: CLI --preview-hints that prints YAML + sample cost delta estimates
integration tests: synthetic trace fixtures and golden expected presets for regression
review_comments: Evan Chu: Can the sampler be further throttled for very large manifests to avoid added latency? Suggest moving sampling to background job — author: added TTL+async worker (see recorder.py) and added canary to validate no upload latency regression.

Lena Bauer: The microdiff JSON schema looks good but we should include a stable fingerprint to allow diffs to be referred to in release notes — author: added microdiff_fingerprint field (sha1 of sorted key-values) and documented in docs/onboarding/hints.md.

Diego Ramos: Are privacy redaction rules sufficient? We should explicitly ban prompt text in traces — author: enforced trimming and added unit test for redaction; CI verifies zero prompt-like tokens in artifacts.
Evan Chu: minor nit: move cost-estimator into a separate helper to reduce coupling — author: refactored estimator to onboard/hints/cost_estimator.py per suggestion.
Lena Bauer: approve after doc tweak — APPROVED
release_notes: Add workload-aware onboarding hints and changelog microdiffs: onboarding now emits suggested profile presets and a short machine-friendly diff for profile/manifest changes. This helps teams choose suitable presets quickly and keeps release notes concise. (opt-in via org feature flag)
notes_for_release_team: This PR introduces new artifacts (hints.yaml + microdiff.json) attached to model manifests. Release packaging should include microdiff summaries for model release emails when present. Ensure orchestration copies hints artifacts to staging storage during rollout.
qa_verification_steps: Enable org flag model_onboard_hints in staging
Upload sample model manifest with synthetic trace (use tests/fixtures/sample_trace.json)
Run CLI: redwood onboard --preview-hints <manifest> and confirm YAML + blurb output
Confirm microdiff.json appears next to manifest in staging bucket and fingerprint matches renderer output
Validate no prompt content present in sampled artifact by running redwood onboard lint <manifest>
